historical_reviews.deepseek: Its inventory can confirm some model/serial/size fields, but it neither authenticates the host safely nor tests the source's negotiated PCIe link requirement.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: Correctly rejects the unsafe transport and restores the missing per-drive PCIe correlation without permitting any storage mutation.

historical_reviews.v3_1: M.2 acceptance requires bijective mapping among physical slot, NVMe controller, namespaces and PCIe BDF. Namespace rows alone can overcount one controller, and LnkCap alone describes capability rather than the negotiated LnkSta; the comparison must therefore use controller identity and actual link state per populated slot.

original_test_intent: Verify every populated M.2 NVMe device's identity, capacity/transport and negotiated PCIe speed/width against the approved platform recipe.
original_method: Authenticate the exact SUT, collect complete block/NVMe controller and namespace inventory, resolve each controller to a physical M.2 slot and PCIe BDF, capture unfiltered `lspci -vvv` link capability and negotiated status per BDF, normalize units and compare every required field with a versioned SPEC without writing or rescanning storage.
manual_activity: The storage/platform owner supplies and approves the physical M.2-to-controller/BDF map, recipe values and disposition of absent, optional or mismatched devices.
required_inputs: Approved M.2 population and SPEC revision
Expected model, serial policy, capacity and transport
Expected PCIe generation and lane width per slot
Verified host-key SSH with secret-safe authentication
Structured parser and unit normalization rules
safety_requirements: Use only read-only inventory and PCI configuration queries
Never expose a password in process arguments or command history
Do not disable SSH host-key verification
Do not format, sanitize, reset, rescan or manage namespaces
Do not infer physical slot from `/dev/nvmeX` numbering
Preserve complete output and exit status
Stop interpretation on ambiguous mappings or incomplete devices
agent_execution_scope: Verify host identity and tool availability
Capture complete per-BDF PCIe identity and link state
Compare normalized fields against the approved recipe
Report mismatches and raw evidence without altering devices
engineer_actions: Approve the physical and logical M.2 map
Approve expected values and optional-device policy
Resolve duplicate namespaces, missing controllers and link discrepancies
Confirm whether downtrained links are acceptable under the recipe

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: `lsblk` and `nvme list` cover inventory but not the source-required PCIe speed/width. `sshpass -p` plus `StrictHostKeyChecking=no` is not acceptable authentication, and the command does not bind each M.2 controller to a BDF.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Over verified SSH, collect complete `lsblk`, `nvme list` and controller identity, then run `lspci -s <approved-BDF> -nn -vvv` for every mapped M.2 controller and compare LnkSta/LnkCap plus inventory fields to the SPEC.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: All M.2 devices, the explicit `<PCIe_Bus>` per-device check and 10-minute source duration remain in scope.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Build a single evidence table keyed by physical slot and controller serial, with namespaces, BDF, vendor/device identity, capacity, transport, LnkCap and LnkSta compared to the recipe.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds secure transport, controller/namespace de-duplication, complete slot/BDF mapping and explicit actual-versus-capability link comparison.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Inventory-only evidence can show the right drive while missing lane downtraining, and BDF-only evidence can show a healthy endpoint without proving it is the expected physical M.2 device.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Commands are read-only, but incorrect mapping can falsely approve the wrong drive; the Agent cannot derive chassis slot identity reliably from volatile Linux enumeration alone.

project_override_considerations: Provide the canonical slot/BDF map for the current riser/backplane and BIOS configuration, capacity normalization, allowed negotiated speed/width states, handling of namespaces and optional empty slots.
expected_evidence: Verified SUT/firmware identity, SPEC revision and physical/logical M.2 map
Tool versions, authenticated SSH details and timestamps with secrets redacted
Complete raw lsblk, nvme list/controller/namespace and per-BDF lspci output with exit status
Per-slot comparison of model, serial, capacity, transport, vendor/device ID, LnkCap and LnkSta
Absent/optional/mismatch disposition, preserved logs, no-mutation audit and engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Procedure and Criteria consistently require M.2 inventory plus per-device PCIe speed/width comparison to a SPEC. The DeepSeek omission is a reference-review defect, not a Master conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The purpose and read-only method are clear. The missing package, map and SPEC are identifiable prerequisites, so classification is REQUIRES rather than BLOCKED.

review_improvement: Restores the omitted link-speed/width requirement and prevents namespace numbering or unsafe SSH shortcuts from substituting for physical M.2 identity.
independent_technical_reasoning: NVMe namespaces are logical capacity objects and do not provide a stable one-to-one physical-drive count. The controller serial and PCIe BDF form the bridge to the physical slot, while negotiated `LnkSta` reveals downtraining that inventory commands cannot see. Only a reconciled mapping can prove both that the expected M.2 device is present and that its actual link meets the platform recipe.
